name: Cortese

lines.s10: Cortese gives Piedmont its crisp white, Gavi: bone dry, with lemon, green apple and a clean, stony finish.
lines.s20: Cortese is the grape of Gavi, from the hills of south east Piedmont that look towards the Ligurian sea. It is light, bone dry and sharp, with lemon, green apple and a stony finish, a wine made to be poured cold with fish.
lines.s45: Cortese makes Gavi, a crisp white from the south east corner of Piedmont, a region known first for its red wine. It tastes of lemon, green apple and pear, with a stony finish and a faint note of almond. It is light and bone dry, and its acidity is high and bright. The winemaking is plain: steel tanks, no oak and an early bottling, though a little is made sparkling. Serve it cold with oysters, raw fish or a plate of fried seafood. Gavi sits just over the hills from Genoa, and its wine has long gone to the fish restaurants of that coast.
lines.sale: Cortese makes Gavi, the cold, bone dry white that has long gone to the fish restaurants of Genoa's coast. I would open it with the oysters and keep the bottle on the table through the fried fish.

glass.lead: Lemon zest, green apple and pear, light and bone dry, with acacia blossom and a stony, faintly almond finish.

ladder.where: The higher hills of Gavi, towards the Apennines
The lower slopes of Gavi and the Alto Monferrato

glass.structure: Bone dry. Acidity high, alcohol moderate, body light; a little is made gently or fully sparkling.

home.home: The south east corner of Piedmont: eleven communes of the province of Alessandria around the town of Gavi, on clay and limestone a short way from the Ligurian coast. Gavi is Cortese alone, mostly still, made in steel and bottled young, with frizzante, spumante and Riserva versions. The grape also grows in the Alto Monferrato and the Colli Tortonesi.
home.abroad: It hardly travels. Beyond Piedmont it has a part in the Custoza blend near Lake Garda, and outside Italy it is scarcely grown.

service.temp: 45 to 50 degrees Fahrenheit, 7 to 10 degrees Celsius: well chilled.
service.glass: A white wine glass; a tulip for the sparkling versions.
service.decant: No. It is a light, crisp white, poured cold and fresh.
service.age: Enjoy most within two or three years; a Riserva is built to keep a few years longer.

labels.means: One wine under either name: Cortese alone, from eleven communes around the town of Gavi.
In full Gavi del Comune di Gavi: grapes grown in the commune of Gavi itself, not a higher rank.
Gavi from lower yields, aged at least a year before release, six months of it in bottle.
Gently sparkling and fully sparkling Gavi, both allowed beside the still wine.

guest.q: What grape is Gavi made from?
guest.a: Cortese, and nothing else. Gavi is the town, in the south east of Piedmont, and the rules allow no other grape in the wine.

guest.q: What does Gavi di Gavi mean? Is it a step up from Gavi?
guest.a: It means the grapes grew in the commune of Gavi itself, one of eleven in the zone. It tells you where the wine is from, not how good it is; the grower matters more.

guest.q: I usually order Pinot Grigio. Will I like this?
guest.a: Very likely. It is just as light and dry, with a little more bite: lemon, green apple and a clean, stony finish. It is at its happiest beside shellfish.

compare.tell: Arneis, Piedmont's other white, is rounder and softer, with pear, almond and lower acidity; Cortese is leaner and sharper, with lemon and green apple.
Pinot Grigio is as light but softer and more neutral, with pear; Cortese has higher acidity, more lemon and a stony finish.
Garganega, as Soave, is softer and rounder, with white peach and a bitter almond finish; Cortese is leaner and more lemony, with green apple.

profile.st: Pale straw · Body light · Acid high · Alcohol moderate · Bone dry, still or sparkling
profile.fruit: Lemon zest, lime, green apple, ripe pear; a hint of white peach from warmer slopes and years
profile.other: Acacia blossom and hawthorn, a faint bitter almond, a stony finish; no oak as a rule
profile.tell: A light, bone dry, high acid Italian white of lemon and green apple with a stony finish and little perfume: Gavi
profile.regions: Gavi in south east Piedmont; Cortese dell'Alto Monferrato and Colli Tortonesi; a part of the Custoza blend by Lake Garda
profile.confuse: Arneis is rounder, with pear and lower acidity; Pinot Grigio is softer and more neutral; Garganega is rounder, with white peach and bitter almond

cards.front: Cortese: which wine does it make, and where is the town?
cards.back: Gavi, also labelled Cortese di Gavi: Cortese alone, from eleven communes of the province of Alessandria in south east Piedmont, near the Ligurian border. A DOCG since 1998.

cards.front: What does Gavi di Gavi on a label of Cortese mean?
cards.back: That the grapes grew in the commune of Gavi itself: in full, Gavi del Comune di Gavi. It names a place, not a higher rank.

cards.front: Cortese blind: what gives a glass of Gavi away?
cards.back: A light, bone dry white with high acidity: lemon, green apple and a stony finish, no oak and little perfume.

questions.q: A guest orders a dozen raw oysters and asks for a light, bone dry white from Piedmont with plenty of acidity. Which bottle do you bring?
questions.exp: Gavi, from Cortese, is light, bone dry and high in acidity, a natural match for raw shellfish. Roero Arneis is rounder and softer, and Moscato d'Asti and a passito are sweet.

questions.q: A blind white is pale and bone dry, light in body with high acidity: lemon, green apple and a stony finish, no oak and little perfume. Which grape is it most likely to be?
questions.exp: Light body, high acidity, lemon and green apple with a stony finish point to Cortese from Gavi. Arneis is rounder, with lower acidity, and Viognier and Gewürztraminer are loudly perfumed.

questions.q: A guest points to Gavi di Gavi on the list and asks whether it is a higher grade than the plain Gavi beside it. What do you tell her?
opts: No: it names grapes grown in the commune of Gavi
Yes: it is the Riserva, aged a year longer
Yes: it must come from older vines
No: it marks the gently sparkling version
questions.exp: Gavi di Gavi, in full Gavi del Comune di Gavi, names fruit from the commune of Gavi, one of eleven in the zone. It is a place, not a rank; the Riserva is the wine held a year before release.

report: Mode home, as the plan fixes it: Gavi in south east Piedmont, with the Custoza blend by Lake Garda given as abroad.

A thin grape: the profile is written in the manner of GRAPES. No Codex record is contradicted. The Codex already holds Gavi as Cortese, lean, dry and unoaked, lemon and green apple with a stony finish, served cold with raw fish and shellfish and built for the seafood of the Ligurian coast; clay over limestone; DOCG since 1998; Gavi di Gavi as fruit from the commune of Gavi; Arneis rounder and less acid, with pear and almond; Cortese in the Custoza blend.
Acidity: INTRO_GRAPES gives Cortese the top of its acidity dial and the Codex calls it high acid, so the entry says high. Some reference pages call it moderate; the Codex stands.

INTRO_GRAPES gives the aroma as green apple, citrus, white flowers and mineral. The entry names them: lemon zest and lime, acacia blossom and hawthorn, wet stone and crushed chalk. Almond, lime and the hint of white peach follow the common account of the grape; hawthorn and acacia are a taster's naming of the white flowers.

The rules (Cortese alone, eleven communes of Alessandria, still, frizzante, spumante, Riserva and Riserva Spumante; Riserva one year with six months in bottle) stand on the production rules as published by the Associazione Italiana Sommelier and by the Piedmont region, read through search results.
The ladder (the higher hills towards the Apennines against the lower slopes) is a taster's reading; no source read sets it out.

Left out: the first written mention of the grape (sources give 1614 and 1659), the legend of the princess Gavia and the story that the grape is named for her courtesy (legend only), Gavi's sale to Genoa in 1202 (one source), and Cortese in the Oltrepò Pavese and Garda (one source).
The line that the wine has long gone to the fish restaurants of the Ligurian coast rests on the Codex's own Piedmont record and Régionale question.
The sources were read through search results; this session could not open the hosts directly.

checked.verdict: Sound after three fixes. Cortese alone, the eleven communes of the province of Alessandria, the DOCG of 1998, Gavi del Comune di Gavi as a place and not a rank, the Riserva from lower yields at one year with six months in bottle, the still, frizzante and spumante types and the grape's high acidity were confirmed.
changed: lines.s45: a region otherwise given to red wine now reads a region known first for its red wine. Moscato d'Asti and Roero Arneis are white wines of Piedmont, and the Codex's own Piedmont record teaches both beside Gavi.

questions[0].q: a light, bone dry white from Piedmont left Roero Arneis, the second option, a fair answer. The guest now asks for plenty of acidity too, which parts Gavi from Arneis as the entry's own tell does.

questions[2]: the stem spelt out Gavi del Comune di Gavi and the key said the commune of Gavi, so the stem translated its own answer. The guest now points to Gavi di Gavi and asks whether it is a higher grade, and the four answers are two of yes and two of no. The explanation keeps the full name.
open: The ladder is borne out in general terms: two trade reports give the red clay of the north of the zone the fuller, fruitier wines and the higher, stonier ground to the south the more delicate ones. Neither names the notes on each rung, which stay a taster's reading.
Lime and hawthorn stay a taster's naming: no page read in this pass names either for the grape, and none speaks against them.
Cortese in the Oltrepò Pavese stays out of the entry: one reference page again, with a second naming only Garda and Custoza.
